Spatial-Intel · world-model probe · 6 Santa moves

A 6.8M-param DIAMOND world model moves Santa where a 4B edit-LoRA can't.

The task: given a game frame and a move action, predict the next frame with the red “S” badge relocated one cell. We tested the same six moves two ways — a FLUX.2-klein edit LoRA, and the real DIAMOND diffusion world model (eloialonso/diamond) trained on just those six.

FLUX.2-klein edit-LoRA

0/6

4B params · region-weighted loss

Copies the input frame or duplicates the badge — never commits the move.

DIAMOND denoiser

5/6 correct

6.8M params · 162s train · EDM diffusion

Relocates the badge and preserves the scene. 4/6 by the blob detector, 5/6 by eye.

Read the images, not the counter. The automatic scorer picks the largest bright-red blob, which sometimes grabs a red present instead of the badge — so it flags one correct move as a miss. The strips below show what actually happened. Why DIAMOND wins: the action enters every UNet block as a FiLM embedding (not a weak text prompt), and the context frame is channel-concatenated (not a copyable input image).

Each strip is input frame · DIAMOND prediction · ground truth, predicted at 64px (blurry but spatially faithful — this is a “does it move correctly” probe, not a quality benchmark). Trained on the six moves themselves, so this measures memorization of the dynamics; held-out generalization is the next test.
